sam (oncall): Heads up — eu-central1 apiserver spike since ~12:03 UTC. CPU ~88-92%, watch cache eviction floods, etcd follower lagging. GPU provisioners started returning 500s for new pods.
lee: On it. I can see a huge fanout from a job called trainer-batch-eu — ~1800 pod/status updates/sec hitting apiserver. watch-cache churn is killing the apiserver CPU.
jordan: Controller-manager is flapping leader election around same time. Logs show repeated lease renew failures: "failed to renew lease: timed out" then crashloop on leader election.
mike: Quick mitigation ideas: 1) throttle trainer job (scale down), 2) temporarily add an apiserver replica in eu-central, 3) reduce controller-manager leader-election frequency a bit or bump lease duration, 4) admission control rate limits. Which do we want first? :thinking_face:
lee: I'll scale apiserver +1 in eu-central now (creating new control plane pod in managed cluster). Also scaling trainer-batch to 1 replica to stop the churn.
deploy-bot: roll/cp-eu-central-apiserver +1 triggered by lee — started rollout 12:12 UTC.
sam (oncall): Scaled trainer down. Pending GPU pods count slowly dropping, some still stuck Pending (0/1) with message: "Failed to create pod: apiserver timeout (watch cache eviction)".
jordan: Controller-manager restarts dropping off after we scaled apiserver. Leader lease renewals succeeded at 12:15. No further crashloops observed.
mike: For near-term config change we should reduce controller-manager --leader-elect-renew-deadline to be more forgiving? Or increase lease-duration? We'll open a RFC. Also need short-term kube-apiserver flag: --watch-cache-size and consider watch-burst-throttle.
lee: We also saw a cost bump because cluster-autoscaler provisioned extra GPU nodes during the spike. Need to add a max-burst cap for GPU pools to avoid repeated overprovisioning during control plane instability.
sam (oncall): Confirming GPU provisioning success rate improving. 12/15 previously Pending now bound. Still monitoring.
mike: Follow-ups: 1) patch trainer-batch to use fewer status updates (reduce requeue rate), 2) add quota/rate-limiter for high-fanout controllers, 3) add transient autoscaler cap for GPU pools, 4) postmortem if this recurs. I'll create tickets.
